stem: A 16-year-old with delayed sleep phase disorder has already tried sleep hygiene, early morning light, gradual wake-time advancement and melatonin, but continues to miss substantial amounts of school; which management option is appropriate for difficult cases?

options.text: Returning to a late sleep schedule on holidays
Routine sedative use as the main next step

explanation: Hospital admission for sleep rescheduling is the appropriate escalation in a difficult case of delayed sleep phase disorder when initial measures have failed and school attendance is being significantly affected.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Hospital-based sleep rescheduling is a supported option for severe refractory delayed sleep phase disorder with major functional impairment.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because hospital admission for sleep rescheduling is a supported escalation for severe refractory delayed sleep phase disorder.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because unrestricted weekend sleep-ins worsen circadian delay and undermine treatment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because reverting to a late schedule on holidays reinforces the delayed sleep pattern.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because routine sedatives are not the recommended main management step for delayed sleep phase disorder.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because management should focus on sleep rescheduling and maintaining school attendance, not stopping schooling.
